users.removeBody: {{email}} loses access to this tenant. Their account and the records they created stay.

impersonate.title: Sign in as {{email}}
impersonate.body: You’ll get a one-time link that signs a browser window in as this user, so you can see exactly what they see. Anything you do there is done as them.

users.subtitle: Every account on the platform, across all tenants.

toast.banned: Account banned and signed out everywhere.

signOut.title: Sign out everywhere?
signOut.body_one: {{email}} is signed out of {{count}} device and must sign in again.
signOut.body_other: {{email}} is signed out of {{count}} devices and must sign in again. Their access tokens stop working within an hour.

resetMfa.title: Reset two-factor authentication?
resetMfa.body: {{email}}'s authenticator is removed, so they can sign in with just their password and set up 2FA again. Only do this after confirming who you're talking to.

confirmEmail.title: Mark the email address as confirmed?
confirmEmail.body: {{email}} can sign in without clicking the confirmation email. Only do this if you're sure they own the address.

ban.title: Ban {{email}}?
ban.body: They're signed out everywhere and can't sign in until the ban ends. Their tenants and records stay as they are.
ban.audited: Recorded in the audit log with your name.

billing.subtitle: Revenue, invoices, subscriptions, plans and coupons, with Stripe and PayPal.
billing.monthlyHint: Money collected, less refunds, all providers.
billing.refundManual: Records a refund you've paid back outside FacilityPro (bank transfer, cash).
billing.refundProvider: Refunds the customer through {{provider}} straight away. This can't be undone.
billing.voidBody: Voiding cancels an unpaid invoice. The tenant no longer owes it.
billing.cancelStripe: Stops the Stripe subscription. The tenant falls back to the Free plan's limits when it ends; nothing is deleted.
billing.cancelPaypal: Cancels the PayPal subscription straight away (PayPal has no end-of-period option). The Free plan's limits apply; nothing is deleted.
billing.cancelAtEnd: At the end of the paid period (recommended)
billing.plansHint: Prices shown to tenants and the limits the database enforces. To sell a plan online, create the matching price in Stripe and plan in PayPal and paste their IDs here.
billing.featuresHint: One per line, shown on the plan card.
billing.providerIdsHint: Leave empty to sell this plan by invoice only.
billing.couponsHint: Discounts for card payments and manual invoices. Coupons are created in Stripe automatically the first time a tenant uses one.
billing.couponLocked: The discount can't change once created; make a new coupon instead.

errors.price: Enter a price of 0 or more.
errors.stripe: Stripe price IDs start with price_.
errors.paypal: PayPal plan IDs start with P-.

setup.webhookHint: Add this address as a webhook endpoint in both Stripe and PayPal.
setup.stripeWebhook: Webhook signing secret saved as STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
setup.stripePrices: Every paid plan has a Stripe price ID
setup.stripePortal: In Stripe, turn on the customer portal (Settings → Billing → Customer portal) so tenants can update cards and cancel.
setup.stripeEvents: Webhook events: checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.created / updated / deleted, invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed, invoice.finalized, invoice.voided, charge.refunded.
setup.paypalPlans: Every paid plan has a PayPal plan ID
setup.paypalLive: PAYPAL_ENV set to live (for real payments)
setup.paypalEvents: Webhook events: all BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION events, PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED, PAYMENT.SALE.REFUNDED, PAYMENT.SALE.REVERSED.
setup.secretsNote: Keys are Supabase Edge Function secrets (Project settings → Edge Functions → Secrets). They're never shown here or sent to the browser.
setup.statusError: Couldn't reach the admin-billing function. Is it deployed?
setup.eventsHint: The last 50 events from Stripe and PayPal.

tickets.macrosHint: Reusable answers for common questions. Insert them while replying.

security.subtitle: Two-factor authentication and sign-in rules for platform staff.
security.yourMfaHint: Use an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password…).
security.require2faHint: Staff without 2FA are asked to set it up before the admin panel opens. The database refuses staff actions from sessions without 2FA.
security.require2faFirst: Verify your own 2FA above first, so you can't lock yourself out.
security.withoutMfa_one: {{count}} staff member hasn't set up 2FA yet; they'll be asked to at their next visit.

security.staffHint: Who can open the admin panel, and whether they use 2FA.

security.passwordNote: Password length and sign-in limits for all users are set in Supabase (Authentication → Policies).

mfa.intro: Add an authenticator app to your account. You'll enter a 6-digit code from it when you sign in to the admin panel.
mfa.scan: Scan this code with your authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code it shows.
mfa.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
mfa.cantScan: Can't scan? Enter this key instead:
mfa.enterCode: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app to continue.
mfa.wrongCode: That code didn't work. Check your phone's time and try the newest code.
mfa.enrolFailed: Couldn't start the setup. Try again.
mfa.active: Two-factor authentication is on for this session.
mfa.gateBody: Platform staff must confirm their sign-in with an authenticator app.

monitoring.subtitle: Is the platform healthy? Background jobs, email delivery, app errors and payment webhooks.

setup.title: Scheduler set-up
setup.hint: What background jobs and email delivery need in Supabase.
setup.cronFix: Turn on pg_cron in Supabase → Database → Extensions; until then no job runs on its own.
setup.netFix: Turn on pg_net in Supabase → Database → Extensions; emails won’t be sent automatically without it.
setup.vaultFix: Add both secrets in Supabase → Project Settings → Vault (see OPERATIONS.md); the email job can’t start without them.
setup.unknownHint: Couldn’t check from here. If the email queue job fails with a Vault message, add the secrets.
setup.uptime: For alerts that still arrive when email is down, point an uptime monitor (UptimeRobot, Better Stack) at the health Edge Function — see OPERATIONS.md.

jobs.title: Background jobs
jobs.hint: Scheduled work the platform does on its own. Staff with Monitoring access get an email when a job is late or failing (at most every 6 hours).
jobs.started: Started {{job}}. Its run appears here when it finishes.
jobs.tooSoon: This job ran less than a minute ago. Try again shortly.

email.topErrorsHint: Most common delivery errors in the last 7 days. Select one to see those messages.
email.noErrors: No failed messages in the last 7 days.
email.retryAllBody: Every message that failed in the last 24 hours goes back in the queue and is sent on the next run (up to 500). Fix the cause first — for example the email provider key — or they’ll fail again.
email.cancelBody_one: {{count}} waiting message won’t be sent. This can’t be undone.
email.cancelBody_other: {{count}} waiting messages won’t be sent. This can’t be undone.
email.privacy: Message contents aren’t shown here because they can hold tenants’ data.

errors.noneOpenHint: Unexpected errors people hit in the app appear here, grouped so each bug is one row.
errors.howItWorks: The app reports unexpected errors (crashes, failed requests) automatically. The same bug is counted in one row. A resolved error that happens again reopens, marked “Came back”. Ignored errors keep counting but stay out of the way. Errors not seen for 90 days are deleted.
errors.workflowsHint: Automation runs that failed in the last 7 days.
errors.noWorkflowFailures: No workflow failures in the last 7 days.

webhooks.resend: A failed webhook is retried automatically by Stripe and PayPal; you can also resend it from their dashboard. Each event is only applied once.
